name: Pressure washer

comps.spec: Petrol engine, 4–7 hp, horizontal shaft (gas models)
Mains universal or induction motor, 1.5–2.5 kW (electric models)
High-pressure axial or plunger pump, about 100–250 bar — sprays, but moves little volume
comps.loc: Bolted to the engine or motor shaft

comps.spec: Braided high-pressure hose, 6–15 m, plus garden hose fittings
Petrol left in the tank (gas models)
Power cord with a built-in GFCI plug on electric models (Sun Joe SPX3000: 35 ft, 10.7 m) — keep it whole
Detergent tank: one on the Predator 62214 and two removable ones on the Sun Joe SPX3000; the Simpson MSH3125 has a soap hose and filter kit instead
Unloader valve on the pump: sends the water round in bypass when you release the trigger (Simpson: no more than 2 minutes in bypass) — leave it on the pump and don't adjust it
Thermal relief valve on the pump: dumps a gush of hot water when the pump overheats (Simpson MSH3125; the Predator warns of very hot water if left idling) — leave it on the pump

notes: Release the pressure in the hose and gun before disconnecting: a high-pressure jet can inject water under the skin.

sources.title: Open Repair Alliance, Open Repair Data v0.3 (community repair events, 2012 to July 2026; CC BY-SA 4.0): 1,583 repairs recorded as Power tool (pressure washer subset)
